resources.string: Original sound (Spatia off for a moment)
Turn on to hear your apps without Spatia, then off again to compare.
Saved separately for each output. Now editing: %1$s
Place the music in a space. The space is added on top, so the original sound is never reduced.
Uses Android\'s built-in reverb on everything the phone plays. Echoes are softer than a real echo, because Android\'s reverb can\'t repeat sounds.
An empty concert hall: a short pause, then a long, warm echo from every wall.
An old single-screen theatre: a vintage, slightly muffled tail and a slap back from the rear wall.
Open air: almost no reverb, a few soft reflections from trees and one distant building.
A small tiled room: bright, dense and close.
A canyon: clear echoes that bounce left and right, then fade.
A huge stone space with a very long, dark tail.
An open arena: a big delayed slap and a wide, washing tail.
A small, lively room with a short punchy tail.
A furnished room: a subtle, natural ambience.
Hard parallel walls: a fast, ringing flutter echo.
Widens the sound so it seems to come from around you, for every app. Uses the phone\'s virtualizer, strongest with headphones.
Quiet parts get louder and loud parts quieter, for low-volume listening.
Restores bass and treble at low volume, following the ear\'s equal-loudness curves.
Import a parametric EQ file (AutoEq or EqualizerAPO text format) to correct your headphones\' frequency response. The file is read once and stays on your device.
A short listening check builds a gentle compensation curve (at most +6 dB). It isn\'t a medical test, and the results stay on this device.

Sit somewhere quiet and set your volume to a comfortable middle level. Don\'t change it during the check. You\'ll hear quiet tones in one ear at a time. Tap \"Heard it\" as soon as you can hear the tone.
Safety for this output: at most %1$.0f dB boost, limiter ceiling %2$.0f dBFS, volume warning above %3$d%%.
Each pair of headphones keeps its own settings. Devices are recognised by type and model name, never by hardware address.
Estimates headphone exposure against the WHO safe-listening guideline (80 dB for 40 hours a week). It\'s an estimate from the volume setting, not a measurement, and it stays on this device.
This week: %1$d%% of the safe weekly dose
Listening at high volume through headphones for long periods can permanently damage your hearing.
The volume is very high. Long exposure at this level can harm your hearing.

Spatia changes the sound of everything your phone plays (YouTube, Netflix, Spotify, games) through Android\'s global sound effects. Apps that announce their audio (many music players) also get their own copy, with a per-app boost below.
Needed for YouTube, Netflix and other apps that don\'t announce their audio. Turn off only if it clashes with another equaliser app.
Your phone isn\'t letting Spatia change all apps yet
Changes here won\'t be heard until the Home tab says Spatia is working. It shows what to do on your phone.
None yet. That\'s normal: YouTube, Netflix and most apps are handled by the global mix instead.
Enhanced with EQ, dynamics and limiter
Basic equaliser only. Boost is disabled because this device has no limiter effect.
Couldn\'t attach. The app or device refused the effect.
Boost is limited to %1$.0f dB for this output and always runs through the limiter.
Your sound settings apply to all apps.
This device or output doesn\'t offer the platform spatializer. Spatia\'s own spatial audio still works.
Available but turned off in system settings.
Available and on for supported multichannel content.
Available through Android\'s reverb for all apps. Echoes are softer than a real echo.
This phone has no reverb effect that can be applied to other apps.
Starts when Spatia is on. Whether your phone allows it shows on the Home tab.
Works for apps that announce their audio session, with a basic EQ only. No boost, because there\'s no limiter.
This device exposes no audio effects to apps.
This phone has no virtualizer effect, so Spatial can\'t be applied to other apps.
Allowed. The system-wide service notification will show.
Denied. System-wide enhancement still works, but its notification is hidden.
Your apps play unchanged. Switch on to apply your sound to YouTube, Netflix, Spotify and everything else.
Attaching to your phone\'s sound output.
Play anything (YouTube, Netflix, music, games) and change a mode or environment: you\'ll hear it right away. Press Play test sound to check.
Your phone\'s own sound effect has control
Another sound enhancer on this phone took over. Turn it off (see the tips below for your phone), then press Try again.
This phone doesn\'t let apps change the global sound, so only apps that announce their audio (listed in the Apps tab) are changed. YouTube and Netflix can\'t be reached on this phone without root.

This phone refused Spatia\'s global sound effects. Turn off the phone\'s own sound enhancer (tips below) and press Try again. If it still fails, this phone\'s software doesn\'t allow changing other apps\' sound.
Fine-tune EQ, environments and spatial in the Sound tab.
Only one sound enhancer can control the phone\'s output. Turn off the phone\'s built-in one and any other equaliser app.
Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO: Settings → Sound & vibration → Sound effects (or Headphones and sound effects) → turn off Dolby Atmos / Mi Sound / Adaptive sound and set the equaliser to Default.
OPPO / realme: Settings → Sound & vibration → Dolby Atmos / Real Sound / Sound effects → Off.
OnePlus: Settings → Sound & vibration → Dolby Atmos (or Audio Tuner / OnePlus Audio) → Off.
vivo / iQOO: Settings → Sound & vibration → Sound effects (Hi-Fi, Dolby Atmos, DTS) → Off.
Samsung: Settings → Sounds and vibration → Sound quality and effects → turn off Dolby Atmos and set Equaliser to Normal.
Keep Spatia running: in app settings set Battery to No restrictions (or Unrestricted) and allow Autostart, otherwise the phone may stop it in the background.
Plays a few seconds of music the same way YouTube or Netflix would. Change a mode or environment while it plays.
Your phone didn\'t let Spatia start in the background. Open Spatia again, or allow Autostart in app settings.
On the phone speaker the effect is weaker; headphones give the widest sound.
Working: changes apply to all apps.
Another sound enhancer on this phone has control.
This phone refused the global mix. Only apps that announce their audio can be changed.
Available through the phone\'s virtualizer for all apps.
